name: Shrinking the short-window span converts redundant attention FLOPs into optimizer steps
statement: Halving the S-layer attention span again (sequence_len//2 -> sequence_len//4) removes attention work whose information the interleaved L layers already provide. Under a fixed training-seconds budget the saved time reappears as additional optimizer steps, and the extra token exposure lowers val_bpb by more than the reduced local receptive field costs.

nodes.label: optimizer steps completed within the 300s charged budget

assumptions.statement: The L layers and the residual stream retain enough distant context that halving the S span does not remove information the model needs.

alternatives: The gain is pure throughput and would vanish at matched step count.
The measured delta is a contended-window artifact rather than the intervention.
predictions: num_steps rises measurably before val_bpb improves.
If num_steps does not rise, val_bpb does not improve either.
falsifiers: val_bpb improves with no increase in num_steps, which would refute the step-exposure mediator.
num_steps rises but val_bpb does not fall, which prices the lost receptive field above the extra exposure.
